prompts: Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: conceptual desktop website screen, 16:9 landscape, high fidelity art direction mockup, not production screenshot. Primary request: Daniel Cantor's developer portfolio as an explorable 3D workshop game. Make a full-bleed believable real-time 3D environment viewed at HUMAN EYE LEVEL just outside the doorway of a contemporary two-storey industrial creative workshop, as if about to enter it. The viewer is standing on the ground, not observing an isometric tabletop diorama. Large open sliding industrial door, warm interior light, central workbench with miniature architectural models of real portfolio projects. Rear rooms and glass partitions leading to project exhibits: teal logistics showroom for Kliniu, refined ivory brand gallery for L'ORIGINE, acoustically treated music studio for 4U Studio Academy, technical network installation for Drokex. Visible human scale stair to archive mezzanine, quiet shelves and tools. Environment occupies the entire browser viewport, integrated diegetic physical signage. No actual people or avatars. No weapons. Style: polished stylized realism, restrained indie exploration game art, beautiful Blender-quality architecture but geometry feasible to simplify for browser GLB. Materials: pale architectural concrete, green powder coated metal, oak workbench, frosted glass. Soft daylight and warm practical lamps, realistic shadows, no neon cyberpunk. Palette: concrete #D7DAD5, deep green #315749, brass #BC9B63, wood #9E7958, graphite #252D29. Overlay typography calm contemporary sans serif, in Spanish, highly legible. Exact visible text top left "Daniel Cantor", below "Full-Stack Developer". Top right subtle text button "Ver proyectos". At lower left aligned title "El taller de Daniel", smaller subtitle "Entra y explora lo que construyo.", solid deep green button "Entrar al taller", secondary text link "Ver portafolio". Small bottom right text "Concepto visual". A tiny physical sign above door reads "Taller". No fake numbers, loading percentages, awards, claims, project screen UIs invented as real. Any computer screens should be blank or abstract non-text representations. Avoid website card grid, giant marketing hero, isometric dollhouse, toy tabletop, HUD clutter, emojis, all caps labels, exaggerated bloom, tiny illegible text. This should convincingly show that the PAGE ITSELF is a 3D place one can enter.

Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: cohesive high fidelity UX concept board with SIX equal landscape screenshot panels arranged in two columns and three rows, high-resolution landscape board, thin neutral gutters, each panel numbered simply in its caption outside its viewport. Primary request: six successive screens of Daniel Cantor's 3D workshop portfolio, a restrained indie exploration game with real rooms at human eye level, same workshop consistent geometry across all panels. Contemporary industrial creative workshop made of pale concrete, green steel, oak and frosted glass, warm daylight, artful stylized realism, Blender-quality visuals. No people, no avatar, no weapons, no neon cyberpunk. Screens: PANEL 1 CAPTION "1. Carga": architectural blueprint line drawing of that same workshop on dark deep green background, title "Preparando el taller", sublabel "Cargando el espacio", thin progress line WITHOUT percent or numeral, bottom link "Ver portafolio". PANEL 2 CAPTION "2. Entrada": looking into actual workshop from open street-level doorway, text "El taller de Daniel", button "Entrar al taller". PANEL 3 CAPTION "3. Exploración": eye-level interior central oak workbench with architectural project models, windows, glass partitions, visible doors labeled "Kliniu", "L’ORIGINE", "4U Studio Academy", "Drokex". Tiny bottom help "Haz clic para acercarte", quiet navigation "Proyectos   Tecnologías   Trayectoria   Contacto". PANEL 4 CAPTION "4. Proyecto": human eye level INSIDE the Kliniu teal logistics-inspired room, shelves, product structure models and computer monitor showing abstract blank product screen, legible HTML-style panel on right occupying only one quarter of view, title "Kliniu", text "Catálogo y cotizaciones B2B", button "Ver caso", link "Volver al taller". This monitor is a symbolic conceptual representation not evidence of actual published product. PANEL 5 CAPTION "5. Tecnologías": a tool wall and an illuminated green shelving area, physical tool-like objects with restrained labels "React", "TypeScript", "Next.js", small readable panel "Tecnologías" and "Ver proyectos relacionados". PANEL 6 CAPTION "6. Móvil": show a flat PORTRAIT mobile viewport centered within this landscape panel, no device mockup frame, same beautiful 3D interior eye-level mobile crop, text "El taller de Daniel", large thumb-friendly bottom button "Ir a proyectos", small next button "Entrar al taller", no joystick. UI language Spanish, use precise text above and no other long copy. All six panels coherent like one product. No fabricated metrics, no loading percentage, no emojis, no fake awards, no lorem ipsum, no excessive HUD, no isometric dollhouse. Make environment itself dominant in every screen and show content as a readable calm overlay. Small label in the bottom board margin "Mockups conceptuales".
correction_prompt: Use case: text-localization. Edit target: the attached generated conceptual workshop entrance mockup. Make exactly one correction: the existing project name on the wall of the teal room on the left is misspelled. Replace that wall sign with the exact name "Kliniu", spelled K-l-i-n-i-u. Keep the sign in the same position and perspective. Preserve everything else pixel-consistently as far as possible: architecture, room layouts, lighting, color, camera, plants, all overlay text and buttons, L'ORIGINE, 4U Studio Academy and Drokex labels. Do not add new text, change the composition or redesign anything. The sole requested change is correcting the left project room label to "Kliniu".
